# gardience_schedule (Resource)

A schedule: runs a runbook or workflow on set days at a set time (a maintenance window).

A schedule runs things on the fleet by itself, so one made with an API key **starts turned off**: an admin turns it on in the console (Automation > Schedules). Changing what or when it runs, or the runbook it runs, turns it off again until an admin looks. `enabled` shows whether it is on now. Changes that cannot be undone (wiping disks, removing the Salt agent) are never scheduled.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Runs the runbook every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 02:30 Central.
# It starts turned off: an admin turns it on in the console (Automation > Schedules).
resource "gardience_schedule" "nightly" {
  id     = "nightly-restart"
  name   = "Nightly nginx restart"
  ref    = gardience_runbook.restart.id
  inputs = { service = "nginx", group = "Linux" }
  days   = ["mon", "wed", "fri"]
  time   = "02:30"
  tz     = "America/Chicago"
}

output "nightly_is_on" {
  value = gardience_schedule.nightly.enabled
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `days` (List of String) Days it runs: `mon` to `sun`.
- `id` (String) Your id for the schedule: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
- `name` (String) Display name.
- `ref` (String) The runbook's or workflow's id, for example `gardience_runbook.x.id`.
- `time` (String) Start time, `HH:MM`.

### Optional

- `inputs` (Map of String) Values for the runbook's form fields.
- `kind` (String) `runbook` (default) or `workflow`.
- `tz` (String) Time zone, for example `America/Chicago`. Default `UTC`.
- `week` (String) Only that week of the month (`1` to `4` or `last`), for example Patch Tuesday plus a week. Unset: every week.

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether it is on now. Only an admin turns it on, in the console.
- `waiting` (String) Why it is off, when it is waiting for an admin.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import gardience_schedule.nightly nightly-restart
```
